approved: Universities Accord (Student Support and Other Measures) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would implement several higher education reforms from the Australian Universities Accord.

It would cap HELP loan indexation at the lower of the Consumer Price Index or the Wage Price Index, backdated to June 2023, and require universities to pass 40 per cent of student services fees to student-led organisations.
It would also create a weekly Commonwealth Prac Payment for about 68,000 teaching, nursing and social work students each year and rename enabling courses 'FEE-FREE Uni Ready Courses'.
Cap HELP indexation to the lower of CPI or WPI with effect from 1 June 2023.
Require higher education providers to allocate 40 per cent of SSAF revenue to student-led organisations.
Establish a grant for a weekly Commonwealth Prac Payment to eligible students in placements.
Rename enabling courses for Commonwealth supported students as 'FEE-FREE Uni Ready Courses' and create a new CGS funding cluster for them.
More than 3 million Australians with HELP debts, around 68,000 teaching, nursing and social work students a year, students from under-represented backgrounds, and higher education providers.

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2024-11-26.207.2) "*that schedule 2 stand as printed*". In other words, they voted to keep it unchanged. This motion took place after Victorian Senator [Sarah Henderson](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/victoria/sarah_henderson) (Liberal) moved that the schedule be deleted. ### What does Schedule 2? According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd2425/25bd008): > *Schedule 2 will require higher education providers to allocate a minimum of 40 per cent of their Student Services and Amenities Fee revenue to student-led organisations. The Bill proposes to define a student led organisation, based upon enrolled students constituting a majority of the governing body of the organisation, enrolled students electing the majority of such members, and satisfying requirements in the Higher Education Support (Student Services, Amenities, Representation and Advocacy) Guidelines 2022.*

The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2024-11-26.226.1) introduced by Victorian Senator [Sarah Henderson](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/victoria/sarah_henderson) (Liberal), which means it failed. Senator Henderson [explained that](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2024-11-26.226.1): > *This concerns the Commonwealth prac payment. It's an amendment which requires the government to table the eligibility and means test requirements for the Commonwealth prac payment before any new grant payment can commence. This amendment is very important because in the bill there is literally no detail about how this payment is going to be delivered. For many stakeholders and higher education providers from whom we heard during the bill inquiry, there is a lot of concern about the nature of this payment because it's not being administered through Centrelink. It's actually being administered via some grant bucket. While we support the prac payment for teaching, nursing, midwifery and social work students, which will apply from 1 July 2025, we are very concerned, and we share the concerns of higher education providers about the way in which this has been proposed and will be administered.* ### Amendment text > *(1) Clause 2, page 2 (table item 9), omit the table item, substitute:* > >> *9. Schedule 4* >> >> *The later of:* >> >> *(a) the day this Act receives the Royal Assent; and* >> >> *(b) the day after draft amendments to the Higher Education Support (Other Grants) Guidelines 2022 specifying extra conditions of eligibility to receive a grant to assist higher education providers to provide payments to students who are undertaking mandatory practicums as part of their course of study are presented to the Senate.* >> >> *However, the provisions do not commence at all if the event mentioned in paragraph (b) does not occur.*
